justification: Changes the checker's verdict for rules printed inside pictures: a rule proven by OCR is served as the council's words, so a wrong proof would show text the council did not print.

pre_impl.existing_data: regulatory_provisions quote_status/quote_reason (migration 111); verdicts stay within the existing values (recovered, reason picture_ocr)
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: OCR may misread; the proof therefore needs every word of 3+ letters and every number, not a share of them
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: applies the next time council_quote runs on a chapter; only rules the text check left unconfirmed are tried
pre_impl.external_source_error: OCR engine missing (rapidocr not installed): the proof is skipped and the rule stays unconfirmed
pre_impl.frontend_type: no frontend change: a recovered rule already shows its quote with the existing note
pre_impl.user_failure_mode: a rule the OCR cannot read fully stays 'Our reading — check the exact wording on page N', never shown as the council's words

functions.name: council_quote_picture.prove
functions.input: the rule's text, the cached chapter PDF path and the rule's stored page number
functions.output: the quote and the page holding the picture when every word and number was read there, else None
functions.if_none: the rule keeps its unconfirmed verdict and its 'Our reading' note on the site

values.value: OCR word set of a page
values.guard_at: None when the page has no picture or OCR is unavailable

queries.purpose: none added: the checker's existing per-chapter judging; OCR reads the cached PDF only
queries.where_clause: unchanged by this change: served rules of one chapter
queries.if_wrong: unchanged: the writer still stores only rows whose text is unchanged

break_it.scenario: OCR reads most but not all words of a rule
break_it.what_happens: a near-miss would be served as the council's words
break_it.how: every word of 3+ letters must be read; one miss leaves it unconfirmed

break_it.scenario: A number differs between the rule and the picture
break_it.what_happens: a wrong setback or height would be shown as the council's
break_it.how: every number must be read, with numbers split from units so 9m checks 9

break_it.scenario: A text page without any picture is OCR'd
break_it.what_happens: the OCR path would prove text the text layer already refused
break_it.how: only pages holding an image are read

break_it.scenario: A two-word drawing label such as 'Rear boundary' reaches the picture proof
break_it.what_happens: a drawing label would be served as a rule

break_it.scenario: none added in the query, but OCR runs for every unconfirmed rule of a big chapter
break_it.what_happens: a large chapter's check would be slow, one OCR per page, cached per page
break_it.how: only unconfirmed rules try it and each page is read once (cache)

falsifiable_check.fails_when: a rule with a missing word or number, or on a page without a picture, is proven
falsifiable_check.observed_red: The number test failed first: '9m' tokenised as one short word, so 9 was never checked; fixed by splitting numbers from units.
falsifiable_check.external_authority: Hornsby pilot 2026-10-12: targeted OCR raised proven rules on pages 1-60 from 89% to 92%.

post_merge.manual_verify: Yes: run council_quote --dry-run on hornsby part 3 and count picture_ocr verdicts
